wp:wtfs-business-angel-4-bullshit-metric.text: In 2013/2014 Inventures asked me to write a series on our experience as a Seed stage fund, about stuff that makes us wonder, but not in a good way. This series originally titled “WTFs of a Business Angel” hasn’t lost its truth it seems, so we decided to revisit the content, update and adapt it where necessary and publish it here on our blog (also because investures.eu sadly is gone from the Web). Have fun! When we started Speedinvest in 2011, we were a startup ourselves. A very well funded startup, but still, we were a team of people who had some experience in building companies and no experience in building a Venture fund. We’re still learning an awful lot, because you can profit tons from other people’s experience, but there is no way around doing things yourself, making mistakes, trying again and again, learning from what you’ve seen so far. That is the spirit that we like to keep, a positive and pro-founder type of attitude, because the truth is: we love what we’re doing. It’s fun and exciting to meet visionary people, who have drive and enthusiasm to change whatever tiny bit of their world, step by step. However, there are those rare events where we sit across the table in our office and have a facepalm moment. When one of us gets an email from a startup or reads a piece of news about our industry that just makes you go “WTF?”. For your reading pleasure, but also to offer you the opportunity to learn, we open up our treasure chest of awkward moments and give you our top WTFs, of course with all due respect to those contributing to them. WTF #4 Bullshit Metrics For very good reasons a lot of startups are shifting towards a metrics-driven approach, meaning that they start looking very closely at values like retention, lifetime value or acquisition costs. This is part of a broader movement to learn from past startup experiences and shift the art of the start a little more towards a reproducible process rather than a piece of luck with some intuition added. Naturally this increases the number of metrics we begin to see in pitches, presentations and reportings. But there is a difference between metrics and bullshit metrics. Let me give you some real world examples: recently we got a reporting sheet from one startup that had a confidence level with a colour coding. Now what a reporting should do is to communicate the status of something that has happened. What would a confidence level of ”orange” mean in that case? Is ”green” good (because confidence is high) or bad (because ”we just don’t know better”)? If having metrics means having some fancy chart in your presentation, then please, don’t. Yes, it makes sense to look at downloads, but it makes more sense to look at registrations, active users, retention in cohorts or even actions of users. And if you have those, then please disclose their full power. Another example we recently saw was a chart that compared the competitive landscape of a company already in business, by using a combined index of the Alexa rank, the PageRank , the registered users and the traffic, all packed into one simple number. The chart had no information on the calculation of the index, the weighing of the factors, let alone a justification of the values used at all. It just made the startup look good. That’s an awkward moment, looking at this kind of chart, asking yourself: ”Why would you put a chart like this into your presentation?”. Andreas Klinger recently posted a rant that goes very well along the lines of this: if you use metrics to support your or others’ reality, then don’t. You don’t need to show us perfect numbers to catch our attention. We know that you’re a startup – numbers can come later. Yes, we want to see numbers, but mostly to know that you care about them as much as we do, to evaluate your path. It’s not always about numbers, but about finding out if we together are on the right or wrong way. Numbers help. But when we work together we want to look at the real thing, not funky charts or cooked up numbers. 0 replies Leave your condolences below Leave a Reply Cancel reply Your email address will not be published. wp:wtfs-business-angel-5-sometimes-miss.text: In 2013/2014 Inventures asked me to write a series on our experience as a Seed stage fund, about stuff that makes us wonder, but not in a good way. This series originally titled “WTFs of a Business Angel” hasn’t lost its truth it seems, so we decided to revisit the content, update and adapt it where necessary and publish it here on our blog (also because investures.eu sadly is gone from the Web). Have fun! When we started Speedinvest in 2011, we were a startup ourselves. A very well funded startup, but still, we were a team of people who had some experience in building companies and no experience in building a Venture fund. We’re still learning an awful lot, because you can profit tons from other people’s experience, but there is no way around doing things yourself, making mistakes, trying again and again, learning from what you’ve seen so far. That is the spirit that we like to keep, a positive and pro-founder type of attitude, because the truth is: we love what we’re doing. It’s fun and exciting to meet visionary people, who have drive and enthusiasm to change whatever tiny bit of their world, step by step. However, there are those rare events where we sit across the table in our office and have a facepalm moment. When one of us gets an email from a startup or reads a piece of news about our industry that just makes you go “WTF?”. For your reading pleasure, but also to offer you the opportunity to learn, we open up our treasure chest of awkward moments and give you our top WTFs, of course with all due respect to those contributing to them. WTF #5 Sometimes we miss out Of all the WTF moments we experience, the ones that annoy us the most are actually those in which we are the cause for a facepalm ourselves . So, yes, this does happen. It is especially the case when we pass up on a startup that we should not have missed out on. I will not go into detail, like Bessemer Ventures recently did with their anti-portfolio . This is also because it hasn’t happened too often yet, as we are a young fund. But I’d like to show you some examples. We had been talking to one startup for a long time. It had come out of our network, there was social proof and a nice product idea but we were not entirely convinced. We discussed it back and forth and weighed in on the arguments. When we finally decided not to invest, we called up the founders only to hear in that very call that they had entered into an agreement to sell the company – for ten times the valuation we had been discussing . Good for them, bad for us. It was only two months into our existence – a lucky moment like this could have given us a nice start. Soon after that, we were talking to a rather seasoned founder. He had come up with a big idea – the idea was actually so big, it was a little frightening . I discussed it with some experts in that field and everyone told me not to touch it. Strange industry, overregulated, similar concepts already existed. We passed. After a lengthy discussion, everyone in our partner group was confident. Two months later, one of the experts I had talked to called me asking whether we had ended up investing. He said he had been following them and totally liked what they were doing. We talked to the founder again, hearing that after only two months they were making 40.000 euros of revenue per month. Strong growth, clearly visible traction . The valuation they got at the next financing round was already double of what we had discussed back then. Yes, sometimes we make very bad decisions. We are subject to all kinds of biases. Sometimes, the discussions that we have internally lead us to misjudgment. We try to set up checks and balances wherever possible to avoid this but it doesn’t work all the time. And we have learned to be careful with trusting experts. So, we have started asking real clients of those companies. We try to make two to three business development calls providing the companies that we like with real business opportunities and to give us a more realistic view of the market. Experts tend to have an overconfidence bias and often can’t judge new ideas because they lack the reference frame or the openness. Clients know what they need because they are either willing to spend money or not. But still, sometimes we look at each other and say ”F&#$, we missed out”. PS: We have our own Anti-Portfolio Channel on our internal Slack, to remind us to stay humble. 0 replies Leave your condolences below Leave a Reply Cancel reply Your email address will not be published. wp:x.text: Resources TechCrunch: Speedinvext x launched Mathias launch blog post Marketplace conference 2018 Speedinvest x – investing in network effects . We are on the mission to fund and operationally support the best European early-stage marketplace startups, empowering them to become category leaders. . Speedinvest x is a Micro VC fund under the Speedinvest-umbrella that focuses on early-stage investments in entrepreneurs who are building tomorrow’s platforms and marketplace-businesses and the technologies that enable them. We have the strong conviction that the “platform trend” is here to stay and has actually just begun: Centralized or decentralized marketplaces will continue to “eat the world” enabled by new technologies in areas that we cannot even imagine today. . While we invest very early, we’re committed for the long-term: We understand that it can take as long as 10 years to build a significant business. Once we’ve decided to back a great team, we want to work together as long as possible and aspire to be a reliable, long-term partner. . . Already convinced and want to pitch us? Submit your deck here ! Our vision: . Become the preferred partner of entrepreneurs building tomorrow’s network effects-driven platforms. Fund Facts Investment stage: Pre-seed, seed and series A What we look for: Initial signs of product-market-fit, i.e. an MVP with some first traction in the form of early adopters A complementary team that is passionate about the challenge that lies ahead and obsessed with finding perfect product-market-fit A clear vision on how to build a sustainable category leader Ticket size: €100k to 1M Our first ticket typically amounts to €500-700k. We like to take a leading role in a financing round and reserve significant capital for follow-on investments. Sector and type: Agnostic (B2B, B2C, B2D or C2C) We are strong believers in the power of network effects in whatever form they might occur and benefit your startup. Target region: Europe & beyond Our main investment focus lies on Europe because that’s where we believe we can support best. Opportunistically, we will consider investments outside of Europe – particularly in North America, where we have a strong network through our office in San Francisco. Why Speedinvest x? We are platform experts. We are platform experts. . Speedinvest x consists of true marketplace aficionados: We are a diverse team of founders, makers, operators, investors and platform-enthusiasts. The whole team eats and breathes network effects. For us, there is nothing better than working together with entrepreneurs to disrupt entire industries with a platform-approach. We provide the knowledge and experience we gained from working with, so far, over 60 great companies and teams such as Lieferando, SpotHero, Couchsurfing, Shpock, Xeneta, wikifolio, StarOfService and TourRadar. . With our optional Growth Partner Program (GPP) we support our teams during operational challenges, and offer them experience, resources and support, e.g. executing local business development in a new market such as the USA. GPP means operational engagement in a line function within the startup, closely tied to milestones and goals upon which the founders and Speedinvest x jointly agree. These tasks are often market facing, top line generating activities performed by senior resources that are usually hard to source for seed-stage startups. . In other words, Speedinvest x is in a position to provide not only a cash investment to the founders we back, but also a significant amount of operational resources. This results in a different level of engagement and involvement than the typical mentoring and intros that founders can usually expect from any quality VC. We have a strong ecosystem. We have a strong ecosystem. Speedinvest x is tightly integrated into the overall Speedinvest platform: Our portfolio companies can rely on the entire Speedinvest partnership as well as our specialized service units Speedinvest Heroes (recruiting) and Speedinvest Pirates (growth hacking & marketing). While Speedinvest x provides vertical support and knowhow (e.g. on marketplaces, platforms, network effects), the overall ecosystem offers horizontal support functions and expertise (e.g. recruiting, growth hacking, business development). On top of that, our focus allows us to leverage the knowhow and expertise we gather in our portfolio: With every new investment our network of marketplace aficionados and experts grows. We encourage the founders and team members of our portfolio companies (the “Speedpack”) to support each other by exchanging knowhow, e.g. through formats such as our annual multi-day Speedpack Insights event, our Speedpack slack or The Marketplace Conference . wp:graduate-program-internship-m-f-speed.title: Speedinvest
wp:graduate-program-internship-m-f-speed.text: About Speedinvest Speedinvest is a leading European venture capital fund for digital startups. With 100M Euro under management, Speedinvest works side-by-side with early-stage entrepreneurs to build great companies. Thanks to our hands-on model, our global partner network and our operations in Vienna, Silicon Valley, Berlin and Munich, we have managed to become one of the main focal points for the European startup community. Speedinvest has successfully invested in companies such as Shpock, Tourradar, Wefox, Bitmovin and Wikifolio. About Our Graduate/Internship Program The six- to twelve-month Graduate/Internship Program is a unique opportunity to gain first-hand insights into the startup and venture capital ecosystem and acquire knowledge in strategy and execution. You will work with the investment team and – depending on your academic background, interest and personal fit – either focus on FinTech & InsurTech or DeepTech & Industry or Marketplaces & SaaS startups or work with our pre-seed unit. Internally, you will be an integral part of our investment team, supporting Partners and Associates in all aspects of their work and thus learn the basics of the daily venture capital business. The program will give you the opportunity to work alongside experienced entrepreneurs on projects which will have a real impact on the business world. You will enjoy a great deal of responsibility and will have the possibility to contribute to a number of exciting projects. Tasks and Responsibilities Analyze and track companies and sectors relevant to our investment thesis. Analyze potential target companies’ business models and KPIs and develop coherent financial models. Perform due diligence on potential portfolio companies, including commercial, financial and operational analyses. Assist Partners and Associates building investment cases for potential deals. Participate in weekly investment meetings and regular workshops with entrepreneurs. Support portfolio companies on specific projects. Assist the team with administrative duties, including fund reporting, pipeline management, applicant feedback, travel schedules, preparation for major events, and other initiatives. Requirements Strong academic performance and extracurricular involvement. Completion of or in the final stage of completion of a university degree, preferably in finance, natural science or engineering. Relevant undergraduate work experience, preferably at a startup, VC or financial institution. Excellent analytical skills, commercial acumen and critical thinking ability. Exceptional communication skills, both written and verbal. Fluency in English. Basic knowledge of German is preferred but not mandatory . Demonstrated research abilities. Strong work ethic and a genuine interest in technology. An entrepreneurial ‘can-do’ attitude. You take initiative! A high level of self-organization and independence. You possess the ability to manage multiple requests, assess priorities and achieve solutions. Coding skills are nice to have. Compensation Full-time position (40h/week) based in Vienna or potentially in Berlin. Salary Vienna: 1150 EUR gross/month. Salary Berlin: 1532 EUR gross/month. wp:business-development-manager-silicon-.title: Speedinvest
wp:business-development-manager-silicon-.text: Speedinvest is a leading European venture capital fund for tech start-ups. We work alongside entrepreneurs to achieve a common goal of building great companies. Due to our global partner network that includes operations in Silicon Valley, we have become a key investment and development hub for Europe’s start-up community. We are involved in early stage investments and specialize in operational support. Our company philosophy states that we only work with projects where we can have a truly purposeful long-term impact, by offering experience combined with the right network. In order to support Speedinvest’s development in the US market we are looking for a Business Developer Manager based in our San Francisco office. The job is an excellent way to gain broad exposure to a range of sectors, and to the requirements for scaling fast growing, venture backed companies. Think of it as McKinsey for startups. Your Responsibilities Hands-on work with startup founders Support them to scale their companies Help them identify and penetrate new markets, especially the US Identify customers and partners, build and manage sales and growth campaigns with State-of-the-Art tools. Create sales pitches, participate in customer meetings, build and maintain client relationships Work with startup teams to identify learnings, adapt sales collateral and the sales process accordingly For this reason, startup experience is highly valued. If you have had your own startup, or have been an early employee and helped scale a company, we definitely want to talk to you. Requirements We are looking for an active, creative expert. We want someone who can design/build products and sell them. Technical skills and or BSc highly preferred. European languages (particularly German) are a big plus. Sales and business development experience required. Product management experience highly desirable. Start-up experience in a key leadership role – founder, CEO, COO. Failure is fine. Willingness and ability to network and build trust with relevant players in the focus industries of our portfolio companies Your personal profile Active networking – do you already have a strong local network? Self-driven and independent. Curious, adaptive & flexible. You prefer new challenges over routines. An entrepreneurial ‘can-do’ attitude facilitated by continuous learning. Ability to juggle multiple projects and work on tight deadlines Ability to digest complex information, form a distinct point of view, and communicate it in a clear and relevant way Compensation: TBD. Please send your resume and application to [email protected] and we’ll be in touch with you! wp:cap-table-debt-refactor-shareholder-b.title: Speedinvest
wp:cap-table-debt-refactor-shareholder-b.text: Some of you might have heard about the concept of Technical Debt , a term coined by Ward Cunningham and extended on by Martin Fowler, that describes the “ extra development work that arises when code that is easy to implement in the short run is used instead of applying the best overall solution .” I figured that this concept doesn’t only apply to coding, but also to investing and the “sourcecode” of your company ownership, the captable. In this post I want to examine the similarities and suggest solutions for refactoring. Let’s look at the original thought first.Technical debt simply means that the decisions you make today add up in your codebase, possibly making future changes much harder, slower and thus more costly to implement. In other words: your decisions create debt that comes at a cost. Of course there are often good reasons for taking a shortcut: when you don’t know the best possible solution, you have to do last minute changes or you have to meet a deadline for business reasons. And even though the perfect solution would be preferable, making it work is more important now. It only becomes a problem when you never repay your debt, and instead accumulate it to the point where you have to deal with it or the software breaks. Your investment rounds can lead to cap table debt Your investor base is actually very similar to your codebase: As a seed investor we often see companies that already did previous rounds, with Angels or FFF , first professional investors, accelerators, etc. Because of pivots, longer development times, customer development, funding reasons, etc. they already have a long list of shareholders in their cap table and have given away a significant portion of equity early on. It’s natural that the older your company is, the more shareholders you will have in your company. However, we often see seed stage companies with 10 – 30 shareholders, which creates additional overhead in every step you take building your company, especially when it comes to raising more money or making important business decisions. Building on the concept of technical debt, I would call it: cap table debt . The more shareholders on your cap table, the more cumbersome it becomes to collect signatures, get power of attorneys, inform everyone and in very crucial moments, when time matters, get feedback or decisions. Even the dynamics of board meetings change with more investors in the room. Managing that is part of the deal, but it gets worse if there are inactive shareholders on the list, if fallouts with investors happen, or if the ratio of equity held by investors versus the team is out of balance. What type of debt to avoid Using Martin Fowlers Technical Debt Quadrant , we can try to structure how we look at cap table debt. He differentiates between deliberate choices and inadvertent “mistakes” on the one hand, and reckless (aka dangerous) and prudent behaviour on the other hand. Below are some of the typical phrases we hear from founders in each case. Reckless Prudent Deliberate “We have to use (more) convertibles with caps now!” “We have to take that money now, deal with it later.” Inadvertent “What do you mean by Investors’ majority?” “We should have selected different investors / co-founders.” Let’s look at the behavior in each quadrant a bit more in detail: Deliberate but reckless choices: we layer convertible notes on top of each other, we avoid priced rounds, but neglect the problems that arise from that funding structure. We raise at an inflated valuation, because we set goals for ourselves that we might not be able to reach, thereby putting ourselves in a difficult position (see this blogpost ). Deliberate and prudent choices: we know we would want different investors, but we have no other option, so let’s take that money now and try to deal with it later (through voting rights). We have to take in a strategic investor, but let’s at least get all rights of first refusal out (see this blogpost ), Inadvertent and reckless: we haven’t even looked at investors’ rights, majority thresholds for important decisions, blocking rights, etc. We never asked our investors whether they have enough money left / reserved for us to do a bridge round if needed. We didn’t agree on proper vesting and good leaver / bad leaver clauses with all founders. Inadvertent but prudent: we have no choice but to accept that this co-founder / investor is inactive. This investor is not helpful for what we are building now, but she was useful back then. Avoiding the reckless choices should usually be possible and common sense. Working with the other outcomes is what is possible and should be done. How to solve it: refactoring your captable Many of the founders we work with have gone through a cap table refactoring. They managed to “clean” up their shareholder base by reaching agreements with people on the cap table. We often help the companies to do that because we have to make sure that the company stays fundable: while the cap table is not the driving force, it’s definitely a hygiene factor that needs to be in order. For many investors broken cap tables are an easy reason to reject, as it’s an uncontestable datapoint and usually will produce headaches down the line. We usually have five ways to deal with it: 1. Combining shareholders through trustee agreements to speed up decision making. This is a straightforward process that creates process overhead for one investor (the trustee), but can be used to ease pain. But beware, this is not a long-term solution. 2. Board or decision thresholds are a common strategy that should be considered in every company after a certain size. This transfers most of the big decisions to the board or cuts out small investors from the decision process. Better than the above, but often only an interim solution. 3. Reaching an agreement with co-founders / investors to get parts or all of their shares for part of the exit price. In most cases inactive people on the cap table will, after some discussions, agree to some form of warrant that guarantees them part of the exit proceeds. That’s better than seeing the company die, when your shares would become worthless. 4. Buying out other people from the cap table is the preferred solution of many shareholders that are affected, but most of the time those “secondaries” are hard to factor into funding rounds and usually only happen if there is massive interest, which rarely is the case if the cap table is broken. If it happens, most of the time it’s at nominal value or a severe discount to the current valuation. 5. The last resort is a downround to dilute those shareholders that can’t or won’t participate in the financing round. As this is a very hostile form of cleaning up a shareholder base it’s difficult, depends on a general agreement and leaves scars behind. It also creates legal risks in case of later exits. No matter what way is chosen: the earlier and more vigorously this is done the better. It’s like removing a bandage: it hurts for a short time, but it’s necessary for long term healing. And it also doesn’t mean that cap table debt should never be incurred. Capital is necessary to grow your company, and sometimes a quick solution can be the right one for the moment. But it means that you have to manage your cap table just as you would manage your codebase. wp:daniel-keiper-knorr.title: Daniel Keiper-Knorr
wp:daniel-keiper-knorr.text: Back to overview Current Portfolio Storyclash Enbrite.ly Daniel Keiper-Knorr Partner From ski instructor and stock broker to startup founder and investor: creating new things and guiding others to excellence runs like a golden thread through his life. ‘New millenium, new enterprise’ thought Daniel, who founded his first company in 2000 . Shortly thereafter, i n 2004, he co-founded 3united, a 3-way merger, which, in early 2006, was acquired by VeriSign for EUR 55m. “Creating things and partnering with beginners to guide them to excellence runs like a golden thread through my life – in business as in private.” From 2007 onwards, Daniel continued to flap his wings a s a business angel and consultant. He invested in five Austrian and Swiss startups. Ambitious as he is, in 2011, he co-founded Speedinvest. As a Partner, Daniel runs investor relations and the fundraising desk and supports portfolio companies with business development. Thanks to Daniel’s great thirst for actio n and outstanding communication skills, Speedinvest has established a broad and versatile network across Europe. Daniel is a passionate skier.

wp:ilia-dubinsky.title: Ilia Dubinsky
wp:ilia-dubinsky.text: Back to overview Ilia Dubinsky Partner Ilia has a strong science and technology background, more than 25 years of experience in building high-tech businesses and venture investing on both sides of Atlantic ocean. After receiving MSc from Moscow Fizteh and a PhD from MIT, Ilia left science for technological and strategic consulting, entrepreneurship and venture investing. As a consultant, he provided technological, strategic and investment advice to major corporate clients in retail, banking, manufacturing, telecommunications and venture and private equity funds. His clients included US and Canadian telecom operators (AT&T, SBC, Qwest, Bell Canada), VC/PE funds (MSDW, Blackstone Group, Battery Ventures), telecom equipment providers (Lucent, Cisco, Phillips, Juniper, EMC2), major retail and investment banks (MSDW, Bank of Boston, Bank of America), and high-tech startups. At the beginning of the 2000s, Ilia built and operated successful consulting and high-tech businesses in the USA. “Being useful beats being independent. I have built startups, taught students and managed companies, developed technologies and commercialized them. In every challenge I look for value that I can create.” After moving back to Russia in 2006, Ilia led the Business Development of Telecom, Technology and Media in Central and Eastern Europe of the International Finance Corporation (IFC), and was a partner of S-Group Capital Management (venture fund), co-founder of several startups and CEO of Infra Technology Company. Before joining Speedinvest, Ilia served as director of the Skolkovo Foundation’s Energy Custer, then built and directed the Center for Entrepreneurship and Innovation of Skolkovo Institute of Science and Technology (Skoltech) – an academic department and office responsible for industry liaison, technology transfer, innovation and entrepreneurship that serve Skoltech and partner institutions. The talent, knowledge and skills to equip young people with technical knowledge and business skills, to awaken entrepreneurial spirits and to foster technology entrepreneurship with global aims – all of that comprises what Ilia took away from the experience he obtained on both sides of the Atlantic.

wp:jeroen-arts.title: Jeroen Arts
wp:jeroen-arts.text: Back to overview Jeroen Arts Principal Jeroen is not only an athletic himself inspired by sports and exploring the limits, he also loves to support and motivate others. Having studied international economics, he joined Global Sports Communication after his study. During his stay at this time company – a management agency representing world class Track and Field athletes – he worked closely with the best athletes of the world through world and olympic championships. After the 2012 London Olympic Games, Jeroen decided to undertake a new breathtaking challenge by launching Deskbookers, an online marketplace for work and meeting spaces in the Netherlands. He led the company as a CEO until February 2017 and spearheaded its internationalization by raising venture capital and growing a talented team of 20+ FTEs. “I get a kick when helping entrepreneurs build companies of the future. After setting up my own company, I joined Speedinvest to fund the next ’Eurocorn’ and support great teams .” Jeroen has been working as a Principal at Speedinvest since December 2017, and is dedicated to building tomorrow’s platforms and marketplace businesses and the technologies that enable them.

wp:anthony-danon.title: Anthony Danon
wp:anthony-danon.text: Back to overview Anthony Danon Principal Anthony caught the entrepreneurial bug while working at a Fintech startup in the Enterprise SaaS cashflow management space. He joined Anthemis in June 2014, where he collected a range of experiences in his first year – from M&A in the payments space to innovation consulting for banks and portfolio support in the VC environment. During the following years at Anthemis, Anthony focused on sourcing, evaluating and executing seed and series A fintech investments, primarily in European companies such as TrueLayer and Tide. Anthony supported startups in areas ranging from milestone planning and strategy, to business development and follow-on capital support. He isalso an active part of Seedcamp’s Investment Forum and a mentor to some of their portfolio companies. “I am a firm believer that entrepreneurs are the ultimate catalysts of positive change. They help overcome society’s biggest challenges by creating these rare win-win outcomes through innovation.” Founders can count on Anthony’s experienced support at any time. He is also involved with ReloadGreece, a charity focused on bridging Greek entrepreneurs with investors and know-how. In his personal life, Anthony used to play semi-professional football and is an active snowboarder and waterskier. His curious mind and passion for travelling has brought him around the world. Anthony is an entrepreneur in spirit and firmly believes that entrepreneurs are the key drivers of tomorrow’s success.

wp:erik-bovee.title: Erik Bovee
wp:erik-bovee.text: Back to overview Current Portfolio Gustav Inkitt Stateless Erik Bovee Partner One of the words that describe Erik best is ‘dedicated’. His career as an international top athlete in epee fencing prepared him for all kinds of challenges. After leaving Oxford University in 1999, Erik was equipped for several strategic tasks: he took on senior operational and strategic roles in a number of telecoms and internet companies and gained tremendous hands-on experience as a founder and executive in the tech industry. Erik was a founder of Digital Mobility, sold to Mobile Media Group in 2002, and European Managing Director of eMeta Corporation, acquired by Macrivision in 2006. “I love working with technical founders, who as kids were dragged out of bed early Saturday morning to go to maths competitions, or stayed up late playing D&D or writing games for Apple IIe when everyone else was going out.” From 2006 onwards, Erik worked for VeriSign and was responsible for enterprise messaging mobile product lines in no place less than Silicon Valley. As a US expert, Erik now oversees US operations as well as corporate and business development activities for Speedinvest’s diverse portfolio companies.

wp:corredoira-jack.title: Santiago Corredoira-Jack
wp:corredoira-jack.text: Back to overview Santiago Corredoira-Jack Business Development Director Santiago is a seasoned European entrepreneur in Silicon Valley, where he co-founded 10darts, a communications platform as-a-sevice (CPaaS), and Onpublico, a citizen journalism community leader in local news in the US hispanic market. His experience in startups and network in the Valley made the Spanish Government choose him to set up their startups incubator in San Francisco. Prior to that, Santiago joined the most successful Spanish startup created in the 2000’s, Lanetro – Zed, taking it from scratch to a pre-IPO status within 9 years. Santiago was one of the four C-class team members that took it from a non-revenue status to generating $500m in yearly revenue, managing 150m users worldwide and having operations in 14 countries. In this company, he set up and launched several new business divisions, including the Global Business Development and the Strategic Partnerships and Alliances, managed the operations in the UK, the largest market, and headed the legal department. “In a startup, you never know where the path to success will come from, but you always need to remember that the longer you keep the office light on, the more chances you have of finding it.” Santiago graduated from law school in Madrid and holds 2 masters degrees from the University of London (LLM) and the IESE Business School (Global Executive MBA). He has enjoyed pitching top-notch Sand Hill Road VCs (including Sequoia, Greylock and Andreessen Horowitz) and has also suffered the vertigo of not having enough cash for the payroll 2 weeks before it is due. A strategic thinker and thoroughly data-driven, Santiago is resilient, very curious, an outstanding communicator, skilled negotiator and trusted advisor. He has been collaborating with Students Rising Above for the last 5 years, where he mentors high school seniors with challenging social conditions and outstanding personal and academic potential. Coming from a large family with 7 siblings, the usual startup chaos makes him feel truly at home and comprehensively challenged.

wp:oliver-holle.title: Oliver Holle
wp:oliver-holle.text: Back to overview Current Portfolio Datapath Investly Wikifolio Oliver Holle CEO, Managing Partner In 1997, long before European pioneers were familiar with terms like “mobile”, “entrepreneur” or “startup”, Oliver, switched from his path towards an academic career – at that time he was working on his PhD thesis in Economics at Columbia University – to launch his first tech startup, creating funny, more or less useful online games. After raising way too much money and spending it all in the first tech bubble of the early 2000’s, Oliver and his team went through long three years of painful battle against insolvency, finally emerging with successful pivot into mobile data. In order to accelerate growth, Oliver merged his company with two other startups into 3united AG to become a highly profitable European leader in mobile content and messaging. The acquisition of 3united by Verisign was not only one of the biggest exits coming from Austria at that time but also took Oliver to Silicon Valley, where he spent two years with one of the most ambitious tech companies of that time. “As a founder, I have been challenged, laughed at, celebrated and plainly ignored. As an investor, I try to be helpful, honest and always – always – respect the founder.” When he returned to Austria he was determined to build a new type of venture fund, defined by his strong belief that seed-stage venture needs a very different model than what he has experienced as a founder and that European founders can win big also in places such as the Valley. Despite warnings from pretty much everyone around, Oliver and his scrappy founder team went on to develop their very unique venture model and, in 2011, eventually raised a tiny micro fund of €10M – this way, Speedinvest was born. Oliver contributes across the portfolio in critical moments when help is needed: fundraising, M&A or simply a time of crisis where calm advise can make a difference.

wp:stephen-croome.title: Stephen Croome
wp:stephen-croome.text: Back to overview Stephen Croome Principal Stephen is a fisherman who found the combination of people, data, creativity and learning how to grow digital businesses too exciting to pass up. He has spent over a decade in every part of the digital economy, from running government digital contracts, to growing businesses in web agencies, designing SEO tools, building products, running digital agencies and then helping startups grow by getting down into the mud with them and executing growth strategies and proving their value. “A good head and a good heart are always a formidable combination.” Nelson Mandela Together with deep marketing experience in search and paid marketing, analytics, CRO and UX, Stephen is also a SCRUM Product Owner and brings these two disciplines together to help startups find Product Market Fit. Stephen holds a BSc in Biology and an MA in Social Media, runs the London Startup Growth Meetup at London’s Google Campus and is experienced in helping eCommerce and SaaS companies find and fix their fundamental issues to help them unlock growth.

wp:melanie-repolust.title: Melanie Repolust
wp:melanie-repolust.text: Back to overview Melanie Repolust Event & Project Management Melanie has gained exciting experience in watching small companies become large. Working in the Austrian telecom industry has shown her how fast small teams and enterprises can grow. This growth process captured her attention. Melanie has been working for Speedinvest from the very early stage on and has always been great at bringing together inspiring minds. “I love organizing events that make both founders and investors happy, and am excited which startups will sky-rock.” With her openness and sensitivity for the people around her, Melanie has a great talent for putting innovative ideas into practice. She has organized numerous thrilling events and has unleashed the potential of various promising ventures. Melanie is passionate about connecting people and their dreams. In private, she enjoys hiking, skiing and cooking the most delicious dishes. Melanie loves having dinner with her friends and spending time on sunny mountainsides or lakes, accompanied by vibrant music.

wp:franz-salzmann.title: Franz Salzmann
wp:franz-salzmann.text: Back to overview Current Portfolio Wefox JimDrive GoStudent Bikemap Adverity Franz Salzmann Partner Cultivating a keen interest in new technologies, Franz had gained profound experience abroad before he joined Speedinvest in 2015. After graduating from Oxford, an important starting point for his career was in 2008 when he joined Deutsche Bank. Following his entrepreneurial spirit, in 2012 , he founded a hardware company in Berlin which came to be known as Noa Technologies Inc. based in San Francisco. “It’s great to accompany strong founders and be on their side when things go right, but also when they go wrong.” Striving for meaningful new experiences, Franz is particularly passionate about mobility projects and genuinely developing his interest in the Blockchain, Insuretech, Fintech, Global SaaS Models, Deeptech and other fields and activities that bear the potential to innovatively change industries and our future. As a Partner, Franz enriches Speedinvest with his specialist expertise and profound tech experience. He is eager to constantly identify and promote new prospects for startups in the tech industry.

wp:florian-obst.title: Florian Obst
wp:florian-obst.text: Back to overview Florian Obst Associate Exploring Florian’s bio, you will find two hearts beating in his chest: one for finance and one for technology. The former was born and raised during his studies at Maastricht University and UC Berkeley as well as during a short-lived detour in investment banking (meh…). Luckily, the voice of reason made him return to his (true) passion for technology. This is why he studied Computer Science at University College London where he joined UCL’s research group focused on Agent-Based Models of Complex Systems of Systems. Merging his two hearts, Florian entered Venture Capital and is now part of Speedinvest’s Industrial Tech team. Florian is based in Munich but you’ll frequently find him in Vienna and Berlin – somewhat analogous to his enthusiasm for both classical music and techno.

wp:valentin-menedetter.title: Valentin Menedetter
wp:valentin-menedetter.text: Back to overview Valentin Menedetter General Counsel Valentin is not your everyday lawyer. His strong background in business development, restructuring, M&A and operations, combined with extensive experience in the marketing and creative industry allows him to structure and tackle even the trickiest deals. Throughout his career, Valentin was able to expand his expertise in setting up and managing multinational teams, leading projects in business and legal environments, negotiating partnerships and developing a business. His field of expertise comprises partnerships, business and shareholder strategies, project management, corporate law, viral marketing – and, the vast expanses of the music and radio industry. Outside of Speedinvest, Valentin enjoys playing records at parties and making people dance…

wp:julia-gremsl.title: Julia Gremsl
wp:julia-gremsl.text: Back to overview Julia Gremsl Office and Project Management Julia is not only Speedinvest’s organizational and creative spirit, but also its driving force. As Management Assistant, she always comes up with innovative and extraordinary ideas, while communicating them flawlessly to everyone around her. Julia is a team player and has an ear for everyone. With her contagious laugh and open attitude, Julia’s presence at Speedinvest is undeniable. Julia has a gift to even include the most quiet souls into conversations. “I am a curious person with a hunger for adventures. Working with creative minds and visionaries motivates me.” Her unique skills in design and creative content production guarantee that Speedinvest is always presented in the most contemporary and refreshing guise – representing unlimited visions and innovative change.

wp:marie-muhr.title: Marie Muhr
wp:marie-muhr.text: Back to overview Marie Muhr Head of Operations Marie has gained profound hands-on experience in building things from the ground up. Not only has she led teams of Communication, Digital Marketing and Customer Care at the major player Samsung Electronics Austria, but also has she worked as Managing Director for independent candidate Irmgard Griss in the Austrian Presidential Electoral Campaign. Within only 1,5 months, Marie co-built a functioning electoral campaign from the scratch, based on a concisely developed campaign strategy and election program. The campaign secured 3rd place for Irmgard Griss in the election ballot with 18,9% of the votes. “The best way to predict the future is to create it.” Accomplishing ambitious goals was nothing new to Marie, who, during her time at Samsung Electronics Austria, supervised the development of the app “Power Sleep” which was nominated for a Cannes Lion. The app’s objective was to use a phone’s processing power to perform scientific research during sleep. As Head of Operations, at Speedinvest, Marie oversees innovative international projects and is eager to drive forward promising ideas and potential. Marie strongly cares about sustainable development and environmental awareness, and thus decided to pursue an additional academic career in Environment and Bio-Resources Management. In her personal life, she is passionate about sports such as yoga and TRX, and cultivates a vested interest in arts. Half Austrian and half French, Marie loves travelling and has so far lived in Paris, Düsseldorf, and Zurich.

wp:felix-faltin.title: Felix Faltin
wp:felix-faltin.text: Back to overview Felix Faltin Head of Strategic Projects Felix loves working where strategy meets execution. With degrees in PPE from Warwick University and a Master of Public Policy from Georgetown, he began his career managing health care reform in his hometown, Vienna, before moving on to develop new service lines for a healthcare corporate across Europe and Asia. “The best startups solve real problems, create good jobs and move us forward as a society. Helping them achieve that is one of the best reasons to get up in the morning.” Most recently, Felix advised the Austrian federal minister of infrastructure on innovation and economic policy. The role gave Felix a bird’s-eye view on technological frontier shifts and the tools to shape them, for example by crafting legislation to allow AV tests on public roads or spearheading the foundation of a €310M research center on semiconductor/sensor integration. He also worked passionately to pass a €185M initiative to support the national startup community. Felix joined this community at Speedinvest, where he focuses on finding and growing deep tech startups. As Head of Strategic Projects, he helps lay foundations for Speedinvest’s future growth. Felix looks back on 20 years of drumming with countless concerts and two record releases and looks forward to his next road trip through Italy.

wp:werner-zahnt.title: Werner Zahnt
wp:werner-zahnt.text: Back to overview Current Portfolio Crate Flexkeeping Hitbox Indoors Senseforce Sipwise Werner Zahnt Partner With over 15 years of experience in the internet and mobile content, application and messaging sectors, Werner has gained deep product management and engineering experience paired with thorough financial expertise. As a curious and hard-working university student, Werner co-founded and was COO of Sysis, a MES service provider with a broad network of clients throughout the manufacturing industries. As a co-founder, Werner played a decisive role in turning Sysis’s focus towards mobile. This came to pass in 2004 with the formation of 3united, a 3-way merger that created a top European player in mobile content. “YOUR success keeps me on the go at day and awake at night. I can still tell you crazy stories about the early dot.com bubble days and the Bay Area.” In early 2006, 3united was acquired by VeriSign for € 55M. Building on the experience of this success story, Werner performs startup due diligence and engages in Speedinvest’s financial and product management.

wp:johannes-ferner.title: Johannes Ferner
wp:johannes-ferner.text: Back to overview Johannes Ferner Associate Johannes pursued a career as a Senior IT Consulting before joining Speedinvest as a DeepTech Associate and Junior Investment Manager for multiple portfolio companies. In his previous role he was developing, planning and architecting enterprise applications for top-tier companies in the DACH region. Having been a lead-developer, frontend-architect and SCRUM Master, he has extensive practical knowledge in building and scaling software systems as well as the corresponding UI/UX necessary. Besides hands-on experience he holds an MSc in Information Systems Management from UAS Technikum Vienna as well as an MBA. On this journey, Johannes came in contact with agile development – namely SCRUM and KANBAN. This agility and the corresponding spirit is what brought to life his passion about startups and eventually him in the ad(venture capital) world. Besides working with extensive tech startups ranging from AI /ML, Blockchain, (Industrial-) IoT, Mobile, B2B SaaS Applications, he loves being in the mountains or joining random sports activities such as kayaking on the old Danube.

wp:joerg-floeck.title: Jörg Flöck
wp:joerg-floeck.text: Back to overview Jörg Flöck Chairman of the Board Joerg is a global citizen and has travelled about 60 countries and lived in six of them. His early passion for investing and technology opened the door to an international career in Financial Services. As a swimmer and basketball player, Joerg developed the competitive spirit which ultimately led him into the Executive Committee of Thomson Reuters in New York. He built his C-Level network socializing with global leaders at the World Economic Forum (Davos), advising the Mayor of Rome and meeting Barack Obama at the White House Press dinner in Washington. As an enthusiastic fan and corporate sponsor of Formula 1, he will never forget co-driving a Porsche GT3 with Nico Rosberg. “I love building high profile teams and help individuals to grow. Investing time in people are the best investments I’ve ever made!” Today, Joerg is eager to bridge the cultural gap between the corporate and start-up world. He is an active business angel and corporate non-executive board director. After many years on the FinTech Investment Committee he became Chairman of Speedinvest in October 2017.

wp:mathias-ockenfels.title: Mathias Ockenfels
wp:mathias-ockenfels.text: Back to overview Current Portfolio MyClubs Stowga Sunlight Mathias Ockenfels Partner Mathias eats and breathes marketplaces: prior to launching Speedinvest x, aSpeedinvest focus fund investing into network effects, he was a General Manager for the German market at Uniplaces, an international marketplace for student accommodation. Before that, Mathias built out the marketplace-practice at Berlin-based Point Nine Capital, an early stage fund focusing on SaaS and marketplaces, where he was a Principal for 4 years. Previously, Mathias led the M&A-department of ricardo Group, then a subsidiary of South African Naspers, that operates several online marketplace, classifieds and auction businesses across Europe. Earlier, he started his career as an Investment Manager at Mountain Partners Group in Zurich where he lead early stage investments in companies such as Lieferando or reBuy. “I network effects: our (Speedinvest) x-men will elevate your startup to the next level! Seeing businesses flourish when network effects unfold is what drives me (…and, let`s be honest, dark chocolate and espresso, too).” Mathias holds a German-French double-diploma from European School of Business Reutlingen and Neoma Business School Reims. Knowing Germany’s capital city like the back of his hand, Mathias now leads Speedinvest`s Berlin office as a Partner at Speedinvest x .

wp:lena-krauzova.title: Lena Krauzova
wp:lena-krauzova.text: Back to overview Lena Krauzova Associate As an Associate, Lena supports Speedinvest with her knowledge of the CEE region. Her experience as an observer and then editor for the Forbes Russia’s technology section allowed Lena to focus on in-depth stories about pioneers in new emerging technological markets. Previous to her work at Forbes Russia, she covered startup- and VC-related topics in articles for the business newspaper RBC. What captured her interest were the success stories of technological startups coming from the CEE region. “In tech journalism I have seen many stories of CEE entrepreneurs who had the courage to start something new. I’m happy to have a chance to do it systematically – with the Speedinvest team.” Lena enjoys operating as an intermediary between founders and markets and is passionate about founders whose dream is to conquer global markets with new, “first-in-kind”, products. She believes her help with storytelling can be supportive for founders, and especially of “deep tech” startups, whose products are sometimes not easy to explain.

wp:markus-steindl.title: Markus Steindl
wp:markus-steindl.text: Back to overview Markus Steindl Head of Finance Markus loves to bring harmony into any chaos and reduce complexity through sound elaborate solutions. As an Austrian certified tax consultant, he feels like the “general practitioner” of his entrepreneurial clients and the first contact for all sorts of questions which are not necessarily tax-related. “I rely on honest and trustworthy relationships.” Markus tries to bridge the highly strategic ambitions of Speedinvest to match with national and international tax and compliance requirements. Markus started his career at KPMG and later joined Austria’s leading electricity provider VERBUND to take care of national and international tax issues and working on mergers and acquisitions.

wp:mana-malaklou.title: Mana Malaklou
wp:mana-malaklou.text: Back to overview Mana Malaklou Controlling & Finance Fond of figures and eager to deepen her numerical skills, Mana studied Software Engineering, but eventually did not find her true passion in coding but in the tricks, questions and enigmas of maths. Mana spent four years working as an Office Manager in a construction company. She went on to work in the finance division of Insurance Broker Vero, and ever since, cultivated her passion for finance. Mana became an accountant and came to love her job in managing a company’s finances. “Never hesitate to take on new challenges.” At Speedinvest, Mana has an eye for detail and, with her ambitious, loyal, precise and responsible attitude, keeps everything under control. In her personal life, Mana is passionate about learning languages and sports.

wp:christopher-zemina.title: Christopher Zemina
wp:christopher-zemina.text: Back to overview Christopher Zemina Associate As an LSE graduate and Master’s student of Accounting and Finance at University of St. Gallen, Chris has gained first insights into Speedinvest as a summer intern. Now, as an Associate, he further develops his genuine interest in Fintech and related areas. Eager to learn something new in his work as much as in his personal life, Chris takes on a personal challenge that matters to him every year, from learning the basics of coding to reading one book each week. “Asked by a colleague about my motivation to work in VC, I realized that I’m entrepreneur first, and investor second.” His curiosity inspires him to benefit from multifaceted experiences: having lived in Austria, Belgium, Canada, Italy, UK, Singapore and Switzerland for at least three months, he became familiar with the peculiarities of different markets and industries. As a dedicated tennis and squash player, Chris is eager to take up any challenge and motivate others to do so.

wp:philip-specht.title: Philip Specht
wp:philip-specht.text: Back to overview Philip Specht Associate Philip started his career as a consultant at Boston Consulting Group, where he worked in various industries and also set up a social venture of BCG. Later he helped with the successful market launch and scaling of a VC funded start-up as CCO of the company. Right before joining Speedinvest x, Philip wrote a book about “the 50 most important topics of digitization”. His book aims to help people who are less familiar with the digital space to better understand some of the most fascinating aspects and most pressing challenges of our time. “Being f ounder-friendly, providing the best support for your startup, and seeing your idea become a big economic castle protected by unbreachable ‘moats’ is our ambition at Speedinvest x.” Now at Speedinvest, Philip works from Vienna and Berlin, but also regularly spends time in his home-city Munich to enjoy the Bavarian spirit and look out for exciting start-up opportunities in southern Germany.

wp:nina-woess.title: Nina Wöss
wp:nina-woess.text: Back to overview Nina Wöss Head of Marketing Nina, a big fan of brilliantly composed music, startups and pop culture, has been active in the startup ecosystem since 2012, when she discovered her passion to work with founders as an investor, mentor and supporter. Before pursuing her MSc in Management at Vienna University of Economics and Business, she fulfilled her dream to live and work in beloved New York and Toronto. Back in Austria, Nina followed her entrepreneurial spirit. Writing for a cultural magazine, Nina further developed her passion for arts, literature and live music and visited 86 concerts a year. Joining Speedinvest as the seventh team member, Nina watched and greatly supported every step of the company’s establishment since the very beginning. As Principal at Speedinvest, she decided to focus on B2C related startups and work with companies such as Inkitt, Flaviar and Tourradar. “Contributing to the construction of the biggest regional seed-stage fund had a unique momentum. I am curious about the transformational potential of startups.” In 2016, Nina co-founded Female Founders, an organization to support women in entrepreneurship, grow the number of successful companies founded by women and to foster the next generation of female opinion leaders. Her creativity, openness and unique communication skills poked her to engage in Speedinvest’s Marketing. As Head of Marketing & Community, she puts her focus on portfolio services and knowledge exchange among founders, to passionately fuel dialogue and mutual growth.

wp:isabel-russ.title: Isabel Russ
wp:isabel-russ.text: Back to overview Isabel Russ Associate Isabel has already gained diverse working experience in five different industries (Tech, Media, Consulting, Logistics, Semiconductor) and six different countries (Germany, USA, Austria, China, Switzerland, Singapore). She loves analyzing and understanding people, businesses and processes around her, and is inspired by smart founders who seek to change these for the better. At Speedinvest, Isabel supports founders that are aiming to build platforms based on network effects in any industry ripe for disruption. “ I love being surrounded by smart and motivated founders and, in general, people who are excited about the future and the potential it brings.” Challenges capture Isabel’s attention, who is eager to try out something new every day: from finding the next unicorn to traveling, hiking up the Kilimanjaro or racing her car – Isabel is unstoppable.

wp:nora-frizberg.title: Nora Frizberg
wp:nora-frizberg.text: Back to overview Nora Frizberg Legal Counsel Having gained legal knowledge and experience in Austria and abroad, Nora has developed a spirit of both internationality and specialisation as a lawyer. Nora spent a year and a half in London, getting her LLM degree in finance and corporate law at the London School of Economics and gaining experience in a reputable London City law firm. Back to Austria, Nora dived deep into the world of finance and capital markets as an Associate at the international law firm Schönherr, where she led and managed international finance transactions. “Putting my competences as a lawyer to use by working with curious and passionate entrepreneurs gives meaning to my practice, because I am part of something innovative, something progressive, something new.” Working as an Associate at the national law firm Doralt Seist Csoklich, Nora led M&A projects and specialized in corporate law – a field in which, combined with insolvency law, she is currently writing her PhD thesis at University of Vienna. In her personal life, Nora enjoys traveling and, during winter time, spends her weekends freeriding in the Styrian alps.

wp:lucanus-polagnoli.title: Lucanus Polagnoli
wp:lucanus-polagnoli.text: Back to overview Current Portfolio Diagnosia Ivary Mikme Playbrush Timeular Lucanus Polagnoli Partner Working as an investment manager for well-known Business Angels sparked Lucanus’ passion for digital disruption. He became an entrepreneur by joining a startup to finally change sides again to become an early-stage investor. Lucanus holds a Master’s degrees in Marketing as well as International Management but made a career in financial consulting which highlights his sound cross-industry background. His career in financial consulting prepared him for all kinds of challenges: With his passion to deep dive into new fields and expertise in corporate development Lucanus took on temporary management positions in varying industries from mining to sport equipment manufacturing or B2B software products, where he gained tremendous hands-on experience how to build international businesses. “As a passionate sailor, I am not only excited to be in the same boat with dedicated entrepreneurs but love racing with you against all odds.” Before joining Speedinvest in 2015 he was Managing Director of whatchado.com that – under his leadership made outstanding achievements: it raised a Seed and Series-A round, grew from 12 to 60 employees and doubled revenues every year. At Speedinvest, Lucanus leads investments in person. While taking a holistic approach across industries Lucanus is leading all hardware and digital health investments like Mikme.com, Timular.com or Playbrush.com* Other then working with founders he loves travelling with his wife and three kids, going to the theatre and writing lyrics.

wp:andreas-schwarzenbrunner.title: Andreas Schwarzenbrunner
wp:andreas-schwarzenbrunner.text: Back to overview Andreas Schwarzenbrunner Principal Andreas has an eye for promising ideas and would literally be eager to start a new business every two weeks. As a former policy adviser in the Austrian Parliament, he not only developed an insatiable passion for politics, but also profound expertise on different economic and technological affairs. One of his main objectives is to support the old economy in becoming more digital. “What drives me most is my desire to try out new things. Good things happen when you don’t plan them. I love interesting people with unlimited ideas and an eye for the bigger picture.” At Speedinvest, Andreas is dedicated to identifying the right Industry 4.0 investments, and actively deploys his know-how to support portfolio companies across different sectors He has been working in the Speedinvest offices in Munich and San Francisco, mentors students and has given inspiring speeches at international panels and other events. Andreas is thus inspiring people in multiple ways: as a city council in his Viennese home district, he is convinced that engaging in different fields and activities makes you see the broader picture.

wp:guzel-gumerova.title: Guzel Gumerova
wp:guzel-gumerova.text: Back to overview Guzel Gumerova Partner Her profound experience in investment banking and transactions, CEE background and competitive spirit make Guzel a versatile FinTech expert. As a Partner at Speedinvest, Guzel brings in important expertise and unleashes the potential of promising tech startups. Back in 1997, Guzel worked as an Assistant Director at CA IB Corporate Finance and developed her knowledge of investment banking. In 2003, she joined Vienna Capital Partners (VCP), a leading independent corporate finance advisor in Central, Eastern and Southeastern Europe. Guzel went on to work as a VP for Business Development at Finstar Financial Group, and, since 2007, has been a Board Member of Dirigio, an independent investment and advisory firm that provides strategic advice to investors, startups, corporations, and asset management firms.

wp:daniel-hoffer.title: Daniel Hoffer
wp:daniel-hoffer.text: Back to overview Daniel Hoffer Venture Partner Daniel Hoffer has experience as a Managing Partner at Crux Capital and Partner at Tandem Capital, both seed stage venture capital firms in Silicon Valley. He is also co-founder and former CEO of CouchSurfing, a travel website with >15 million members across every country and city in the world, and a former Entrepreneur in Residence at Benchmark Capital. In addition to entrepreneurial experience he has deep product management expertise from executive product roles at NortonLive (Symantec) and TripIt (Concur/SAP). Daniel has appeared on the cover of Inc. Magazine and been featured on the front page of the Boston Globe, as well as on ABC Nightline, NBC News, National Public Radio, and in the New York Times and Time Magazine. He has also been a guest lecturer at Stanford GSB, Harvard Business School, Kellogg School of Management, and the Haas School of Business at U.C. Berkeley. He is a graduate of Harvard College and Columbia Business School. His “loves” are martial arts, adventure travel, and of course his two daughters and wife.

wp:marcel-van-der-heijden.title: Marcel van der Heijden
wp:marcel-van-der-heijden.text: Back to overview Current Portfolio Cyberwrite Marcel van der Heijden Partner

wp:alex-zhigarev.title: Alex Zhigarev
wp:alex-zhigarev.text: Back to overview Alex Zhigarev Partner With over 15 years of experience in strategy, operations and entrepreneurship, Alex knows сhallenges faced by technological startups and how to deal with them. Having completed a Masters Degree in Applied Mathematics from Moscow Engineering Physics Institute, he started his career as a software developer and project/program manager in large IT companies (Luxoft, Dell, Ericsson). He developed an avionics software, managed process improvement initiatives, was responsible for due diligence cases and M&A in engineering and TMT industries and even evangelized agile methodologies before Agile became a mainstream practice. “ The thrill of creating something new defined my career, from a geeky avionics software developer, to a corporate executive and a high-tech entrepreneur and investor. I am happy that I can bring in my experience, spanning over multiple industries. ” After obtaining an MBA from INSEAD in 2010, Alex moved to the exciting and unpredictable world of entrepreneurship. He co-founded and managed a number of companies, some of which were successful and some less so. The “airbnb” for Russian speaking markets was one of the largest online apartment rental players on the CIS market by 2012. The “Booking.com” for medical tourists collapsed after the crush of the Russian currency in 2014. The gig he worked on before becoming partner of Speedinvest was Vest Financial – a company backed by Y Combinator and First Round Capital and acquired by Chicago Board Options Exchange in 2016. Alex is an angel investor in a number of startups and works on board of one of the largest online travel agencies in Russia.

wp:nina-ehrenreich.title: Nina Ehrenreich
wp:nina-ehrenreich.text: Back to overview Nina Ehrenreich Controlling & Finance As a finance enthusiast with profound long-term experience in the venture capital landscape, Nina brings order into the complex realm of Speedinvest. Nina has taken on challenges of controlling, accounting and administration at various companies. Working at GCP Gamma Capital Partners, managing company of numerous venture funds, she learnt more about the interplay of investing. “It is exciting to observe the successes and challenges faced by both entrepreneurs and investors. Just like I am watching my own three little ‘startups’ grow at home ;)” At Speedinvest, which she joined in May 2015, Nina does not only bring in her expertise, but also brightens up everyone’s day with beautiful flowers. Her colleagues would say that apart from her quantitative, numerical skills, Nina is caring, reliable and dependable and one of her strength is the diplomatic way to find solutions that work for all parties involved, even if that means extra work for her.

wp:severin-zugmayer.title: Severin Zugmayer
wp:severin-zugmayer.text: Back to overview Severin Zugmayer Associate Severin, mainly growing up in Vienna and the Salzkammergut, has always been eager to meet inspiring people from all over the world. He lived in Oslo, Wroclaw and Hamburg where he gained professional work experience in executive search at Kienbaum, brand marketing at Red Bull, as well as sales and marketing at Google. “I love people who are serious about their work but don‘t take themselves too seriously. Seeing startups from different angles has motivated me to take a seat at the investor’s table.” With a growing interest in the startup ecosystem, Severin’s work allowed him to engage with startups and visionary founders from numerous perspectives. At Speedinvest, he is dedicated to follow the development of each portfolio company with utmost accuracy to uncover their full potential. One of Severin’s interests comprise everything human centered around business success like design thinking , allowing him to develop a comprehensive understanding of the most complex situations. Apart from his professional life, Severin loves climbing, skiing, mountaineering and especially team sports like basketball. He is passionate about rare oldtimers and sneakers, knowing all different kinds of them – however only collecting the latter – until now.

wp:stefan-klestil.title: Stefan Klestil
wp:stefan-klestil.text: Back to overview Current Portfolio Iyzico KOIN Loot Tradico Billie Cashpresso Curve Fincompare Stefan Klestil Partner Building on 20 years of professional experience in international payments and banking technology, Stefan has an eye for potential. In his specialist discipline of FinTech investments across EMEA, Stefan is eager to support founders on business and product strategies, bizdev and corpdev. He seeks to identify the best teams in Europe to create the next generation of financial services unicorns, developing new models in factoring and lending, risk underwriting, banking and payment infrastructure, security, cryptography and blockchain. “Working with founders, I can leverage 20 years of international experience in financial technology. Top FinTech founders are seeking smart growth capital, and that’s what we provide. But always, at the heart of a good collaboration, is mutual respect.” Before joining Speedinvest, Stefan has worked as Advisor, Executive, Incubator and Investor. He holds Masters Degrees from Columbia University and Vienna University of Economics and Business Administration and is a non-executive Board Member of Wirecard, Iyzico, Curve and payworks and Advisory Board Member of N26, Wefox, Billie, Fincompare and Loot. Stefan also supports the founders of Fraugster, Tradi.co and Cyberwrite. He is a regular speaker at Money 2020 in Europe and Asia, member of the Money 2020 Academy and selected for the Lattice 80 FinTech Europe 200. Previously, he was President for Central and Southern Europe at First Data, Partner at Roland Berger, and Principal at A.T. Kearney based in New York and Vienna.

wp:vision.title: Get the Idea
wp:vision.text: Revolutionizing European Venture Capital Get the Idea "Speedinvest is the most important startup I ever did." — Oliver Holle + -

wp:arnaud-bakker.title: Arnaud Bakker
wp:arnaud-bakker.text: Back to overview Arnaud Bakker Associate Arnaud has gained professional experience at J.P. Morgan both in corporate banking and investment banking in the healthcare sector, in Amsterdam and London respectively, before joining Speedinvest as an Associate in the pre-seed team. With a growing interest in entrepreneurship and startups, he decided to apply his experience and knowledge to support founders to grow their business. At Speedinvest, he is responsible for sourcing, evaluating and executing pre-seed investments, primarily focused on the healthtech space. “New defendable tech that has the potential to shake up and redefine an entire industry such as the healthcare sector excites me. I love meeting founders who are vision-driven and are not afraid of getting their hands dirty at the same time.” In his personal life, Arnaud used to be a semi-professional swimmer and loves kitesurfing and wakeboarding which he can combine with his passion for travelling. He is also passionate about restoring vintage cars and motorcycles, having participated in several long-distance rallies across Europe and Africa.

wp:elisabeth-grosschaedl.title: Elisabeth Großschädl
wp:elisabeth-grosschaedl.text: Back to overview Elisabeth Großschädl Operations Manager Elisabeth grew up in Styria where the foundation of her grounded and heart-in-the-right-spot personality was built. Her sense for culture and design led her to several places to experience different ways of life – always trying to see things through a habitants lense. After selecting Vienna as her new homebase, she finished her studies in Economics and Business Administration and represented the Austrian Government in foreign economic policy in Brussels, Geneva and Washington DC. Her intuition for trending topics then led her to a political startup. She participated in the development team of independent candidate Irmgard Griss in the Austrian Presidential Electoral Campaign, which started campaigning from scratch. Being passionate about conceptualizing und creating projects, she subsequently joined the Business Riot Festival’s team as head of operations. “I love to explore, develop and build – independently of given structures and directions.” At Speedinvest, Elisabeth can bring her experience as an entrepreneur, her background in economics and her talent to keep cool into top form. Apart from her work life, she’s designing her own art of living between city and countryside – including cultural literacy, social engagement and herbage distillery. She is a congenial hands-on person – with a contagious smile. If she’s not drafting a brand new experience, she brings a project plan to life!

wp:yuliya-kvetko.title: Yuliya Kvetko
wp:yuliya-kvetko.text: Back to overview Yuliya Kvetko Analyst Yuliya is a cosmopolitan per definition: born in Ukraine, but lived, studied and worked throughout her career in the UK, Germany, Austria, China, and Switzerland, Yuliya’s drive for mobility and international exchange is steadily growing. Following this mentality, Yuliya is currently studying her 5th language. The UK has been a home for her, both professionally and personally. She has pursued an MSc in Management, Organisations and Governance at the London School of Economics and Political Science as well as a BSc in Business and Management at King’s College London. Yuliya has gained professional experience in M&A at a Viennese Investment Banking Boutique, as well as in startup operations and business development at a Berlin-based startup. Apart from her passion for the Fintech environment, she is bringing banking and M&A experience to Speedinvest – inspired by a collaborative culture and global focus.

wp:philipp-stangl.title: Philipp Stangl
wp:philipp-stangl.text: Back to overview Current Portfolio Parkbob Fleksy Packpin Timeular Deckard Telleroo Medicus OurPath Blubblub Codeberry TalkJS Cloudo Investory HiMoment ThinkSono Doctorly IOMED Philipp Stangl Head of Pre-Seed Program Philipp, eager to bring to life great businesses, started his first company in the food e-commerce space. Together with his team, Philipp achieved to make KochAbo grow from 0 to 7-figure revenues with a footprint in four European countries. The VC-funded company was exited to Marley Spoon in 2015. Philipp’s experience is built on management consulting roles. He advised clients in the telecommunication and aviation industry and analyzed various startup business models while working for a startup incubator. In his current role as Head of Speedinvest’s Pre-Seed Program, Philipp invests in around 15 digital pre-seed startups a year. The fund currently comprises around 30 portfolio companies, which, on top of the investment amount, benefit from exclusive access to the Speedinvest network in various industries. As a pioneer himself, Philipp is on the advisory board of several portfolio companies in the field of mobility, productivity and digital health. He is actively involved with startups working on mobile apps and SaaS products that are often supported by machine learning and other big data technologies in the backend.

wp:viviane-huber.title: Viviane Huber
wp:viviane-huber.text: Back to overview Viviane Huber Junior Office Manager and Team Assistant Making everyone at Speedinvest feel welcome and cared for is one of Viviane’s greatest aims and skills. While studying German and Biology for teaching, she also discovered her passion for office management and creative business. Viviane or Vivi, as her friends prefer to call her, is highly empathic and open-minded while operating in a very precise and structured way. “Be kind, be passionate, be thankful. I hope that it helps me to work better with these ideals.” At Speedinvest, she supports the general management and is eager to cut thr ough t he clutt er to se e exactly what nee ds to be done. Viviane does not fear any challenges but meets them with great enthusiasm: in her free time, she cultivates a passion for rock climbing and bouldering and is a big nature-lover.

wp:ruth-heinisch.title: Ruth Heinisch
wp:ruth-heinisch.text: Back to overview Ruth Heinisch Office and Project Manager Ruth has gained profound working experience in tourism. Her great eye for detail and the bundle of factors that secure customer satisfaction are valuable skills she has mastered. In the course of her education at the Austrian Academy for Advertising, Ruth has learned a lot about Marketing and Customer Support. She knows how to handle Office Management like the back of her hand, due to significantly contributing towards her father’s plumbing company from childhood on. “A well functioning office constitutes a solid ground for building up startups. Process optimization is my true passion – so let’s make most of it together.” Ruth has developed a strong hands-on mentality and maintains a clear view of all matters. She has obtained a Business Administrations Degree as well as completed a training course of Service Design. Before joining Speedinvest, Ruth has supported the European Forum Alpbach for seven years.
